name: Bell's Palsy
summary: Most people recover, and physiotherapy supports gentle facial exercise, eye care, education and protection against synkinesis; medical review is needed to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes.

looksLike: Onset and facial weakness pattern (forehead involved or spared)
Facial symmetry at rest and in movement
redFlags: Forehead spared (suggests a central cause such as stroke)
Limb weakness, speech or swallowing difficulty or severe headache
Rash with ear pain (possible Ramsay Hunt syndrome)
Inability to close the eye with pain or redness
firstSteps: Confirm that a doctor has examined the patient and excluded other causes.
Assess facial symmetry, eye closure and function, and teach eye care.
Teach gentle mirror exercises and massage.
selfCare: Sun and wind protection for the eye

stages.label: Start: assess and set up
stages.goal: Bell's palsy affects one side of the face including the forehead; if the forehead is spared, think of a central cause and refer urgently.

moveOn: Baseline recorded: Sunnybrook Facial Grading System

stages.label: Treat: build capacity
stages.goal: Eye protection is the most important early task, because the eye may not close.
when: Baseline recorded: Sunnybrook Facial Grading System
do: Slow, small, symmetrical facial movements in front of a mirror
dose: Facial movements: 5 to 10 small, slow repetitions of each movement, 2 to 3 times a day.
Eye closure and blinking: several times through the day.
Facial massage: 5 minutes, 2 times a day.
Relaxation of overactive muscles: as needed.
moveOn: Progress from small to larger movements as control returns

stages.label: Progress and self-manage
stages.goal: Gentle, small, symmetrical exercise supports recovery, while forceful exercise can encourage synkinesis.
when: Progress from small to larger movements as control returns
do: Sun and wind protection for the eye
dose: Progress from small to larger movements as control returns.
Avoid overuse if synkinesis appears and seek specialist advice.
Review at regular intervals and refer if no improvement.
